details: CONFIRMED by reading: bin/relay:685 `relay queue take <slug> -C <worktree>`; delegate SKILL.md step 2 places the step "before
the build", after the brief and worktree exist, and its not-reproduced branch names no release. Correct for the owner's message
(the front brings it), but the queue shows a taken item that nobody works on until the owner answers. Cheap to fix in the same
evidence: plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:119-122 "no build; the item is held for the front, who brings all such items to the owner in one message"
failing_case: The front takes the bench item (`relay queue take <slug> -C <worktree>` needs the worktree, so the branch exists), writes the
brief, and at step 2 a runner finds the failing case no longer fails. The skill says "no build; the item is held for the front".
The item stays "taken by wt/<task>" in `relay queue` and its worktree and branch stay; nothing says to release them. It should
either be reproduced before the take (a read from the main checkout needs no worktree) or be released when held.
fix_hint: "Run it before `relay queue take`, from the main checkout (a read, a command, a test of master)"; or add "release the item
(`relay queue release <slug>`) and remove the worktree" to the not-reproduced branch.
pass_cases: 1. The skill says the reproduce step runs before `relay queue take` (or says a held item is released with `relay queue release <slug>` and its worktree removed).
2. A reproduced claim: taken and built as now.
3. An item with failing_kind test or run: taken and built as now.
reason: tests/test_premise.py:78 asserts "before `relay queue take`" in the delegate skill; text present at SKILL.md step 2.
findings.summary: the reproduce step sits after the item is taken in a worktree, and a held item is never released, so it stays taken by a dead branch
